''10. A man that is an Heretike.''] {{outside R|Who is properly an Heretike, & who is not.}}Not euery one that erreth in religion, is an Heretike, but he onely that after the Churches determination, vvilfully and {{ls}}tubburnely {{ls}}tandeth in his fal{{ls}}e opinion, not yelding to decree of Councel or the cheefe Pa{{ls}}tors of the Church therein. ''They'' ({{ls}}aith S. Augu{{ls}}tine ''ep. 162''.) ''that defend their {{ls}}entence (though fal{{ls}}e and peruer{{ls}}e) vvith no {{ls}}tubburne {{ls}}tomake or ob{{ls}}tinate hart, {{ls}}pecially if it be {{ls}}uch as them {{ls}}elues by bold pre{{ls}}umption broched not, but receiued it of their deceiued parents, and do {{ls}}eeke the truth vvarily and carefully, being ready to be reformed if they finde it, {{ls}}uch are not to be reputed among Heretikes''. And againe, ''li. 18 de Ciuit. c. 51''. {{outside R|De{{ls}}criptions or markes how to know an Heretike.}}''They that in the Church of Chri{{ls}}t haue any cra{{ls}}ed or peruer{{ls}}e opinion, if being admoni{{ls}}hed to be of a {{ls}}ound and right opinion, they re{{ls}}i{{ls}}t ob{{ls}}tinatly, and vvil not amend their pe{{ls}}tiferous opinions, but per{{ls}}i{{ls}}t in defen{{ls}}e of them, are thereby become Heretikes, and going forth out of the Church, are counted for enimies that exerci{{ls}}e vs''. Againe ''li. 4 de Bapt. cont. Donat. c. 16. He is an Heretike that, when the doctrine of the Catholike faith is made plaine and manife{{ls}}t vnto him, had rather re{{ls}}i{{ls}}t it, and choo{{ls}}e that vvhich him {{ls}}elf held &c''. And in diuers places he declareth that S. Cyprian, though he held an errour, yet vvas no Heretike, becau{{ls}}e he vvould not haue defended it after a general Council had declared it to be an errour. ''li. 2 de bapt. c. 4''. So Po{{ls}}{{ls}}idonius in the life of S. Augu{{ls}}tine {{outside L|''Vit. Aug. c. 18''.}}reporteth, how, after the determination of the See Apo{{ls}}tolike that Pelagius opinion vvas heretical, al men e{{ls}}teemed Pelagius an Heretike, and the Emperour made lavves again{{ls}}t him as again{{ls}}t an Heretike. Againe S. Augu{{ls}}tine {{ls}}aith, ''He is an Heretike in my opinion, that for {{ls}}ome temporal commoditie, and {{ls}}pecially for his glorie and principalitie, coineth or els foloweth fal{{ls}}e or nevv opinions''. de vtilit. credendi cap. 1. {{outside R|The former markes agree to the Prote{{ls}}tants.}}Let our Prote{{ls}}tants behold them {{ls}}elues in this gla{{ls}}{{ls}}e, and vvithal let them marke al other proprieties that old Heretikes euer had, and they {{ls}}hal finde al definitions and markes of an Heretike to fall vpon them {{ls}}elues. And therfore they mu{{ls}}t not maruel if vve warne al Catholike men by the vvordes of the Apo{{ls}}tle in this place, to take heede of them, and to {{ls}}hunne their preachings, bookes, conuenticles and companies. {{outside R|Their bookes, {{ls}}eruice, & preaching mu{{ls}}t be auoided.}}Neither neede the people be curious to knowe vvhat they {{ls}}ay, much le{{ls}}{{ls}}e to confute them: but they mu{{ls}}t tru{{ls}}t Gods Church, vvhich doth refute and condemne them. And it is ynough for them to knowe that they be condemned, as S Augu{{ls}}tine noteth in the later end of his booke de here{{ls}}ibus. And S. Cyprian {{outside L|''Ep. 52. nu. 7''.}}{{ls}}aith notably to Antonianus demaunding curiou{{ls}}ly vvhat here{{ls}}ies Nouatianus did teach: ''No matter'', quoth he, ''What here{{ls}}ies he hath or teacheth, vvhen he teacheth vvithout'', that is to {{ls}}ay, out of the Church.

By his owne iudgement.''] {{outside R|Heretikes cut them {{ls}}elues frō the Church.}}Other greuous offenders be {{ls}}eparated by excommunication from the communion of Saincts and the fellovv{{ls}}hip of Gods Church, by the {{ls}}entence of their Superiors in the {{ls}}ame Church: but Heretikes more mi{{ls}}erable and infortunate then they, runne out of the Church of their ovvne accord, and {{ls}}o giue {{ls}}entence again{{ls}}t their ovvne {{ls}}oules to damnation.

{{dropinitial|H}}earing of Philémons vertue, vvho vvas a Colo{{ls}}{{ls}}ian, he vvriteth a familiar letter from Rome (being pri{{ls}}oner there) about his fugitiue {{ls}}eruant One{{ls}}imus: not doubting but that he might commaund him, yet rather reque{{ls}}ting that he vvil forgiue him, yea and receiue him as he vvould Paul him {{ls}}elf, who al{{ls}}o hopeth to come vnto him.
